chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The one who has washed the dead body performs ghusl, and everyone who touches a dead body must perform ghusl, even if the dead body has already been washed.

Because what this report contains in his statement, ‘even if the dead body has already been washed,’ is to be understood as a form of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement. We have already treated in full what relates to that in the book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām, and there is sufficient discussion there, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; a non-obligatory but encouraged ruling
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl; the ritual bath required or recommended in this context
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: performs ghusl; undertakes the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory for someone who touches a dead body after it has already been washed?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of ghusl for one who washes a deceased person and for one who touches a dead body. It also clarifies that the phrase concerning contact after the deceased has already been washed is understood as indicating recommendation rather than obligation, with further discussion referred to Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.
